rv.q: But that underwhelming element turns out to be among the frustrating production’s chief disappointments.
Mr. Nighy, to put it bluntly, mops the floor with Ms. Moore.
Moore's Broadway debut and first New York stage appearance in 14 years - is a crushing disappointment.
Too bad it's in the service of Hare's time-wasting curriculum.
If the evening doesn’t fully satisfy as theatre it is nonetheless jam packed with tasty ideas.
But if Hare is trying to suggest the difficulty of assigning moral worth and blame, the result here is merely confusion.

cn.t: David Hare's Iraq War drama disappoints critics as sluggish and verbose despite a stellar cast. Moore is miscast, though Nighy impresses, and Mendes' direction can't salvage the unfocused, underdeveloped material.
